title.fa: چرا روان‌شناسیِ پیش از روانکاوی ناهشیار را ندید
title.en: Why pre-analytic psychology missed the unconscious
title.nl: Why pre-analytic psychology missed the unconscious

summary.fa: فروید می‌گوید مانع یک فرضیه بود، نه کمبود مشاهده: این‌که فعالیت روحی همان فعالیت آگاهانه است. او این فرضیه را «ظاهراً عملی و در اصل غیرمعقول» می‌خواند و با یک مشاهدهٔ روزمره ردش می‌کند — فکری که بی‌مقدمه به ذهن می‌رسد، مقدمه‌ای داشته که ما از آن بی‌خبریم.
summary.en: Freud argues the obstacle was an assumption, not a lack of observation: that mental activity just is conscious activity. He calls the assumption "apparently practical and at bottom unreasonable" and refutes it with an everyday observation — a thought that arrives without warning had premises we knew nothing of.
summary.nl: Freud argues the obstacle was an assumption, not a lack of observation: that mental activity just is conscious activity. He calls the assumption "apparently practical and at bottom unreasonable" and refutes it with an everyday observation — a thought that arrives without warning had premises we knew nothing of.

text.fa: فرضیهٔ مسدودکننده: «پیش از روانکاوی، روان‌شناسی راه خود را برای رسیدن به دنیای "نهاد" با اتخاذ فرضیهٔ خاصی مسدود کرد. این فرضیه ظاهراً عملی و صحیح به نظر می‌رسد، ولی در اصل غیرمعقول است.»
text.en: The blocking assumption: "before analysis, psychology blocked its own road to the world of the id by adopting a particular assumption. The assumption looks practical and correct, and is at bottom unreasonable."
text.nl: The blocking assumption: "before analysis, psychology blocked its own road to the world of the id by adopting a particular assumption. The assumption looks practical and correct, and is at bottom unreasonable."

text.fa: محتوای فرضیه: «تمام فعالیت‌های روحی از روی آگاهی و هشیاری کامل صورت می‌گیرند و اعمال ذهنی هنگامی ذهنی و فکری تشخیص داده می‌شوند که در هشیاری و آگاهی باشند» — و اگر در مغز جریانی از روی ناهشیاری رخ دهد، «چنین اعمالی شایستهٔ داشتن نام فعالیت روحی نیستند و به روان‌شناسی هم ارتباطی نخواهند داشت».
text.en: Its content: "all mental activity takes place in full consciousness, and mental acts are recognized as mental only when they are conscious" — and if some process occurs unconsciously in the brain, "such acts do not deserve the name of mental activity and have nothing to do with psychology."
text.nl: Its content: "all mental activity takes place in full consciousness, and mental acts are recognized as mental only when they are conscious" — and if some process occurs unconsciously in the brain, "such acts do not deserve the name of mental activity and have nothing to do with psychology."

text.fa: رد فروید با یک مشاهدهٔ در دسترس: «اندکی توجه به شخص خود کافی است آشکار کند پاره‌ای اوقات افکاری در ذهن انسان خطور می‌کند که نمودشان بدون مقدمه امکان‌پذیر نبوده است. اما شما از این مرحلهٔ مقدماتی — که آن قسمت نیز طبعاً می‌بایستی جزو فعالیت‌های ذهنی شما باشد — بی‌خبرید و فقط نتیجهٔ کامل‌شدهٔ آن به ذهن هشیار شما می‌رسد.»
text.en: Freud’s refutation from an observation ready to hand: "a little attention to oneself is enough to show that thoughts sometimes occur to a person whose appearance without premises would have been impossible. Yet of that preliminary stage — which must itself have been part of your mental activity — you know nothing, and only its finished result reaches your conscious mind."
text.nl: Freud’s refutation from an observation ready to hand: "a little attention to oneself is enough to show that thoughts sometimes occur to a person whose appearance without premises would have been impossible. Yet of that preliminary stage — which must itself have been part of your mental activity — you know nothing, and only its finished result reaches your conscious mind."

text.fa: و پاسخ به تبیین جایگزین: محقق می‌گوید «شاید دقت شخص در آغاز به جای دیگری معطوف شده و به آن علت متوجه مراحل مقدماتی نشده است»؛ فروید این را «دوپهلو صحبت کردن» می‌خواند، چون همین پاسخ می‌پذیرد که آن مراحل بوده‌اند و فقط آگاهی به آن‌ها نبوده.
text.en: And his reply to the alternative explanation: the interlocutor says "perhaps the person’s attention was elsewhere at first and so he did not notice the preliminary stages"; Freud calls this "speaking both ways," since the answer already concedes that those stages existed and only awareness of them was missing.
text.nl: And his reply to the alternative explanation: the interlocutor says "perhaps the person’s attention was elsewhere at first and so he did not notice the preliminary stages"; Freud calls this "speaking both ways," since the answer already concedes that those stages existed and only awareness of them was missing.

text.fa: نکتهٔ پدیدارشناختی که همین‌جا می‌آورد: بیمار ممکن است متوجه شود «قسمتی از افکار او می‌بایستی مانند رازی فاش‌نکردنی از شخص خودش هم پنهان بماند»، و آن وحدتی که همیشه برای شخصیت خویش قائل بود دیگر وجود ندارد — «انگار چیزی در او هست که می‌تواند بر ضد خودش تمام شود».
text.en: A phenomenological point he makes here: the patient may notice that "part of his thoughts must remain hidden even from himself, like an undisclosable secret," and that the unity he always ascribed to his own personality no longer holds — "as if there were something in him that can work against himself."
text.nl: A phenomenological point he makes here: the patient may notice that "part of his thoughts must remain hidden even from himself, like an undisclosable secret," and that the unity he always ascribed to his own personality no longer holds — "as if there were something in him that can work against himself."

text.fa: فروید این کشف را «معرف پیشرفت بزرگ دانش روان‌شناسی در مبحث خودشناسی» می‌خواند — یعنی ادعا دربارهٔ خودشناسی است، نه فقط دربارهٔ درمان.
text.en: Freud calls this discovery "the mark of a great advance of psychological science in the matter of self-knowledge" — the claim is about self-knowledge, not only about treatment.
text.nl: Freud calls this discovery "the mark of a great advance of psychological science in the matter of self-knowledge" — the claim is about self-knowledge, not only about treatment.

text.fa: این استدلال نشان می‌دهد پردازش ناهشیار وجود دارد، چیزی که روان‌شناسی شناختی امروز هم می‌پذیرد؛ ولی از آن نتیجه نمی‌شود که محتوای ناهشیار همان است که روانکاوی توصیف می‌کند. این دو ادعا در این رساله از هم جدا نشده‌اند.
text.en: The argument shows that unconscious processing exists, which cognitive psychology also accepts today; but it does not follow that the content of the unconscious is what analysis describes. The two claims are not separated in this essay.
text.nl: The argument shows that unconscious processing exists, which cognitive psychology also accepts today; but it does not follow that the content of the unconscious is what analysis describes. The two claims are not separated in this essay.
